# `generator-shortcuts`

**Strongest plausible shortcut.** Treat color 8 as the only impassable wall.
Start a multi-source cardinal BFS from every color-2 cell, allow traversal through
every pixel whose value is not 8, and recolor reached cells 3/4/5 by distance
modulo three. This wrong rule fits all `5/5` usable canonical pairs because every
canonical barrier is color 8.

**Exact disagreement input.** This is an ordinary emitted sample from final
generator SHA-256
`4a7acdbf7f6e9e36969e843b410bbb746252739953a686634f42e8983fd8cac6`,
with seed `123`, sample index `1`, shape `9x9`, one seed, and wall color `6`:

```text
000000000
066666660
060006060
060006260
060006060
060006060
060006060
066666660
000000000
```

The intended rule preserves the color-6 frame and recolors only the seeded right
chamber. The shortcut treats 6 as traversable, crosses the frame, and recolors
the exterior and wall cells. The two outputs differ in 76 positions.

**How checked.** I saved the input in `checks/shortcut-color8/input.json` and ran:

```text
cwd: repo
python3 ../run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 9199b47fab1e --input ../checks/shortcut-color8/input.json --out ../checks/shortcut-color8/racket.json
```

The command exited 0 and executed selected rule hash `b0749d721740`.
`checks/shortcut-color8/counterexample.json` contains the exact Racket output,
rival output, hashes, validator result, and first disagreements.

**Does the repaired generator emit such cases?** Yes. Two of every three
consecutive samples use wall color 6, 7, or 9. In the final independent census,
the color-8-only rival survived the individual scheduled wall-8 draws (`43/128`
per band) but survived `0/400` complete three-demo windows and `0/1,600`
hold-one-out query rotations. The larger public lesson census likewise found
`0/300` ambiguous ordered lessons and `0/1,200` ambiguous rotations.
